external_entities.name: reader
external_entities.description: A person who accesses the public site and fetches assets from the CDN.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Public site: readers hit the web server over HTTPS, some of them signed in.

external_entities.name: admin
external_entities.description: An administrator who maintains the database directly.
external_entities.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
external_entities.notes: The admin's location is unspecified: they do it from wherever they happen to be.

external_entities.name: CDN
external_entities.description: The content delivery network from which readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

processes.name: web server
processes.description: The public-facing server that runs the CMS and pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

processes.name: CMS
processes.description: The content management system running on the web server.
processes.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS

data_stores.name: MySQL database
data_stores.description: The database holding pages, accounts and comments.
data_stores.source_excerpt: keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database
data_stores.notes: The source says, 'I could not tell you whether the database is encrypted on disk.'

data_stores.name: CDN's bucket
data_stores.description: The bucket used by the CDN to hold published images, stylesheets and downloads.
data_stores.source_excerpt: the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket

data_flows.name: reader to web server site access
data_flows.description: A reader accesses the public site.
data_flows.source_excerpt: readers hit the web server over HTTPS

data_flows.name: web server to MySQL database content access
data_flows.description: The web server stores and accesses pages, accounts and comments in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: The web server runs the CMS and keeps pages, accounts and comments in a MySQL database

data_flows.name: reader to CDN asset fetch
data_flows.description: A reader fetches images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Readers fetch those from the CDN over HTTP.

data_flows.name: web server to CDN's bucket asset publish
data_flows.description: The web server pushes newly published assets to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When new assets are published the web server pushes them up to the CDN's bucket.
data_flows.notes: The source says, 'Nothing here tells you how the push to the CDN is authenticated.'

data_flows.name: admin to MySQL database direct maintenance
data_flows.description: The admin directly maintains the database rather than using the CMS.
data_flows.source_excerpt: There is an admin who maintains the database directly rather than through the CMS.
data_flows.notes: The connection is described as unsecured, with no TLS, from wherever the admin happens to be, and with no jump host.

trust_boundaries.name: public internet
trust_boundaries.description: The external network from which readers access the public site and from which the admin connects from an unspecified location.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: they do it from wherever they happen to be

trust_boundaries.name: hosted network
trust_boundaries.description: The hosted network containing the web server, CMS and MySQL database.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: a MySQL database on the same hosted network

trust_boundaries.name: CDN
trust_boundaries.description: The external service boundary containing the CDN and its bucket.

assumptions.assumption: The web server is reachable from the internet because it serves the public site to readers over HTTPS.
assumptions.basis: The source calls it the 'Public site' and says readers hit the web server over HTTPS.

assumptions.assumption: The MySQL database contains confidential data because it stores accounts and comments in addition to pages.
assumptions.basis: The source states that the database keeps 'pages, accounts and comments'; accounts and comments may contain information whose disclosure harms people or the business.

assumptions.assumption: The CDN's bucket contains public data because it serves images, stylesheets and downloads fetched by readers.
assumptions.basis: The source says readers fetch images, stylesheets and downloads from the CDN.
